text: Introspection [Lat. intro , within, + spectus , seen]: Ger. innere Wahrnehmung , Selbsbeobachtung ; Fr. introspection , observation interne ; Ital. introspezione , coscienza riflessa in sè . Attention on the part of an individual to his own mental states and processes, as they occur, with a view of knowing more about them. Locke uses the term reflection for 'the notice which the mind takes of its own operations' ( Essay , ii. chap. i. § 4). Other writers speak of an 'inner sense' or 'inner perception.' The suggested analogy to 'outer sense' and 'outer perception' is misleading. Literature : see INTROSPECTIVE METHOD. ( G.F.S. - J.M.B. )
